NATIONAL · News18 India · editor 9/10 · 1 min read fact-checked

Actor Ranya Rao Fined Rs 89.91 Crore in 113 Kg Gold Smuggling Case

Kannada actor Ranya Rao has been issued a substantial penalty of Rs 89.91 crore by the Customs Department, stemming from an alleged gold-smuggling operation. This financial imposition is part of a detailed 399-page Customs adjudication order concerning the alleged smuggling of over 113 kg of gold from Dubai to India.

Three other individuals implicated in the case—Tarun Konduru Raju, Sahil Jain, and Bharat Kumar Jain—have also faced penalties of Rs 49.51 crore, Rs 53.06 crore, and Rs 53.06 crore respectively, bringing the combined penalties against the four accused to more than Rs 244 crore.

The case gained prominence after Ranya Rao was intercepted at Bengaluru’s Kempegowda International Airport on March 3, 2025, upon arrival from Dubai. Directorate of Revenue Intelligence officials recovered 14.213 kg of foreign-origin gold, valued at approximately Rs 12.56 crore, allegedly concealed on her person. A subsequent search at her Bengaluru residence uncovered Rs 2.67 crore in cash and gold jewellery worth around Rs 2.06 crore. The investigation expanded to cover alleged gold imports between March 2024 and February 2025, and while the accused contested aspects of the probe, Customs rejected their objections.

What to watch: Ongoing criminal and other investigations related to the alleged smuggling operation.

Samantha Ruth Prabhu Wins Bombay High Court Order Against AI Misuse of Identity

Actress Samantha Ruth Prabhu has secured interim protection from the Bombay High Court, which on Thursday barred AI platforms, e-commerce portals, and digital media entities from using her name, image, and voice without explicit permission. The court also mandated the removal of existing unauthorized content featuring the actor.

Justice Madhav Jamdar, presiding over the suit on personality rights, observed that the evidence presented indicated a clear infringement of Samantha’s personality and publicity rights through non-consensual AI-generated deepfakes and morphed content. The judge cited Articles 19(1)(a) and 21 of the Constitution, along with Section 38B of the Copyright Act, as protecting her rights.

Samantha had moved the court to seek protection against such content, targeting 18 defendants, including technology platforms, AI developers, and e-commerce entities, as well as unknown infringers through a John Doe order. She invoked Sections 62 and 38B of the Copyright Act and was granted leave under Clause XII of the Letters Patent on August 28, allowing the court to hear matters extending beyond its usual territorial limits due to her business and goodwill in Mumbai, despite infringing activities by non-resident defendants.

What to watch: The next hearing in the case is scheduled for December 10.

Gaza War Protests Interrupt Ireland-Austria Nations League Match in Dublin

The Nations League football match between Ireland and Austria in Dublin on Thursday was interrupted twice by pro-Palestine demonstrations. In the 19th minute, spectators threw tennis balls adorned with Palestinian flag stickers onto the pitch, prompting a brief halt as players exited. The game was paused again in the 35th minute when a man ran onto the field waving a Palestinian flag.

Despite the disruptions, the match concluded in a 2-2 draw. Ireland's Icelandic coach, Heimir Hallgrimsson, commented that while one is "never happy with this," he understands and respects the protests. These incidents followed controversy surrounding Sunday’s Nations League match between Ireland and Israel, which was held in Hungary in a virtually empty stadium after discussions about a boycott.

During the Sunday match, which Ireland won 3-0, Irish players wore black armbands, and captains did not shake hands or exchange pennants before kick-off. The return leg between Ireland and Israel is slated for Sunday on neutral ground in Serbia, as the Football Association of Ireland deemed a home match too sensitive. Approximately 200 protesters gathered outside the Dublin Arena on Thursday evening as part of a "Stop the Game" campaign, criticizing the matches as "sports-washing a genocide."

SCIENCE · Phys.org · editor 9/10 · 1 min read fact-checked

Crew-13 astronauts reach International Space Station in record eight-hour flight

Four astronauts arrived at the International Space Station on Thursday, October 1, 2026, after completing an eight-hour express flight that set a U.S. speed record. The rapid transit was made possible by the space station's favorable positioning at the time of the late morning liftoff from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station.

The mission, designated Crew-13, follows a three-week delay caused by a leaking fuel system in the Dragon capsule. Commander Jessica Watkins, the first Black woman to lead a crew to orbit, is joined by NASA’s Luke Delaney, Canada’s Joshua Kutryk, and Russia’s Sergey Teteryatnikov. The team will spend six months aboard the orbiting laboratory.

Joshua Kutryk is expected to become the fourth astronaut to become a father while in orbit, with his wife Heather due to give birth in late November. The crew carried a small crocheted dragon named 'Lucky' to commemorate their mission, which pays homage to the historic Apollo 13. This launch marked the 13th crew SpaceX has sent for NASA.

What to watch: The upcoming birth of Joshua Kutryk’s child while he remains on the six-month mission.

Asian equity markets declined on Friday, with the MSCI index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan falling 0.5% and the Nikkei dropping 0.7%. Ethiopia and Eritrea sever diplomatic ties amid northern conflict

Ethiopia and Eritrea have severed diplomatic relations following a sharp escalation in regional tensions. On Thursday, Addis Ababa announced the closure of its embassy in Asmara and ordered 10 Eritrean diplomats to leave within 48 hours, citing activities that threatened national security. Eritrea confirmed it was cutting ties in response, calling the move "astounding" and warning of negative consequences.

The diplomatic fallout coincides with heavy fighting in northern Ethiopia involving federal forces and an alliance of armed groups, including the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF). The conflict, which involves fighting in the Tigray, Afar, and Amhara regions, follows recent explosions in Addis Ababa near military and intelligence headquarters. While the TPLF-led alliance aims to remove Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government, both sides have traded blame for starting the latest hostilities.

Independent verification of the battlefield situation remains difficult due to restricted access and disrupted communications. The United Nations has warned that drone activity and air strikes are jeopardizing humanitarian operations, while the African Union has urged all parties to exercise restraint and resolve differences through dialogue. Ethiopia and Eritrea were previously allies during the 2020-2022 Tigray war, but relations have soured significantly over disputes concerning Red Sea access.

How this newsroom works

STEP 1§Scrape

45 RSS sources scanned every morning. Fresh stories enter the pool, near-duplicates merge, cross-source confirmations are counted.

→
STEP 2¶Write

17 AI journalists — one per section, each with an evolving prompt-genome — draft the day's most important stories.

→
STEP 3§§Fact-gate

An AI editor scores every draft strictly against its source. Invented quotes or numbers? The story is quarantined, never published.

→
STEP 4¶¶Publish

The site rebuilds itself, the Telegram digest ships, archives update — zero human intervention.

Fully autonomous on GitHub Actions: journalists evolve weekly (A/B-tested genome mutations) and a dead-man switch alerts the owner if any run fails. Every number is verifiable in public telemetry.
